docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Certificate Authority (CA) platform is a multi-tenant system for operating a private Public Key Infrastructure (PKI). This guide is organized as a configuration workflow — follow the steps in order to go from an empty system to issuing certificates.

The platform has two portals:

Portal Audience URL pattern Tenant Super Admin Platform operators who provision tenants https://admin.<domain> Tenant portal PKI operators within one tenant https://<subdomain>.<domain>

Screenshots are illustrative. Names shown (e.g. Root CA 01, Sub CA 01, CA Administrator, example.com) reflect a sample environment and will differ in yours.

docs.title: Dependency at a glance
docs.text: Connectors → Crypto Sources → Templates → Root CA → Sub CA → Validation Authority → Profiles → Request/Issue → Manage. Each step's page lists its Prerequisites.

docs.title: Sign in to the Super Admin Portal & Multi-Tenancy
docs.text: Platform Setup. This is the first step of the end-to-end configuration flow.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The CA system is multi-tenant: one deployment hosts many isolated customer workspaces ("tenants"). The Tenant Super Admin portal is the control plane where you provision and govern those tenants — before any PKI configuration can happen, a tenant must exist here.

Who should use it: platform operators who run the CA service for multiple tenants.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Open https://admin.<your-domain> and sign in with a Super Admin account. On success you land on Administration → Tenants.

docs.title: Tenant Isolation Model
docs.text: Aspect Behaviour Data isolation Each tenant's data lives in its own database schema (t_<subdomain>). Tenants never see each other's CAs, certificates, operators, or logs. Routing Each tenant is reached at its own subdomain — https://<subdomain>.<your-domain>. Identity Super Admins authenticate against a global account store (no tenant binding). Tenant operators are scoped to one tenant. Provisioning Creating a tenant provisions its schema, seeds an admin role + permissions, and creates the first tenant administrator in one transaction.

docs.title: The configuration flow at a glance
docs.text:
Sign in (this page) → Verify license → Create a tenant → Super admins → Sign in to the tenant → … → build access control, cryptographic foundation, templates, CA hierarchy, validation, and issuance. Follow the workflow pages in order.

Important Notes

  • Module availability (CA, VA) and the multi-tenant capability are controlled by the installed license — see License Management.

docs.title: Verify License & Modules
docs.text: Platform Setup. Prerequisite: signed in to the Super Admin portal.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Before provisioning tenants, confirm which product modules (CA, VA) and capabilities (e.g. multi-tenant mode) the license enables, and check usage against limits. Modules that the license does not enable are hidden from tenants.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Administration → License

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• License Overview — Customer, License ID, Machine ID, Valid From/To, Days Until Expiry, Grace Period, and a status badge.
  • Licensed Modules — enabled modules (e.g. CA, VA).
  • Capabilities — feature flags such as Multi-tenant mode: Enabled.
  • Licensed Usage — current vs limit for Tenants, Administrators, Operators, Certificate Authorities, Active Certificates, Roles, API Keys.
  • Tenant Usage — per-tenant resource breakdown.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text: • Upload License — install a new license file (opens the operating-system file picker).

docs.title: Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Open Administration → License.
  2. Confirm Licensed Modules include the modules you need (CA and/or VA).
  3. Check Capabilities shows Multi-tenant mode: Enabled.
  4. If updating entitlements, click Upload License and choose the vendor file.

Important Notes

  • Capability gating: the tenant portal hides modules the license does not enable — absence of a menu item may mean "not licensed", not "removed".

Warning

Uploading an invalid/expired license can disable modules system-wide. Verify the file and validity window before uploading in production.

docs.title: Create a Tenant
docs.text: Platform Setup. Prerequisite: a valid license with the required modules and multi-tenant mode enabled.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Provision an isolated tenant workspace and its initial administrator. Every PKI configuration step that follows happens inside a tenant, so this is where real setup begins.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Administration → Tenants

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• New tenant button, search, status filter, pagination.
  • Table — Subdomain, Name, Tenant admin, Status, Created, Actions (Edit, and a row Actions menu). Each subdomain has a Copy tenant URL button.

docs.title: Row actions
docs.text: For an active tenant the actions menu offers Suspend and Delete (a suspended tenant shows Reactivate). Deleted tenants are read-only.

docs.title: Fields — Create Tenant dialog
docs.text: Field Description Required Notes Tenant name Human-readable name Yes — Subdomain Tenant subdomain / slug Yes Cannot be changed later. Lowercase letters, digits, hyphens. Max CAs / Max certs / Max operators / Max API keys License quotas Yes Blank = Unlimited. Max roles License quota No Optional. Username / Email Initial tenant admin Yes Created in the same transaction. Full name Initial tenant admin name No — Password / Confirm password Admin password Yes ≥12 chars, 1 uppercase, 1 digit, 1 special character.

docs.title: Tenant Detail (quotas & limits)
docs.text: Open a tenant's Edit link to adjust name, quotas, and the per-tenant request rate limit; the subdomain is read-only.

docs.title: Step-by-Step — Create a tenant
docs.text:
1. Open Administration → Tenants.
  2. Click New tenant.
  3. Enter Tenant name and Subdomain (permanent).
  4. Set the required quotas (blank = Unlimited).
  5. Fill the initial tenant admin username, email, and a compliant password.
  6. Click Create.

Important Notes

  • Best practice: choose subdomains carefully — they are immutable.
  • Blank quota means Unlimited, not a default.

Warning

Delete is tenant-wide; use Suspend for temporary lockouts.

docs.title: Manage Super Admins
docs.text: Platform Setup. Prerequisite: signed in to the Super Admin portal.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Super Admins are system-level accounts that administer the CA service across all tenants. This page manages who holds that privileged access.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Administration → Administrators

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Add Administrator button, search, status filter, pagination.
  • Table — Email, Name, Status, Created, Actions.

The per-row actions menu offers Delete.

docs.title: Fields — Create Administrator dialog
docs.text: Field Description Required Notes Username Login username Yes — Email Address Administrator email Yes — Full Name Display name Yes — Password / Confirm Password Account password Yes Minimum 12 characters; ≥1 uppercase, digit, special character.

docs.title: Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Open Administration → Administrators.
  2. Click Add Administrator.
  3. Enter username, email, full name, and a compliant password.
  4. Click Create.

Important Notes

  • Best practice: keep at least two active administrators to avoid lockout.

Security Warning

Super Admins have system-wide privileges across every tenant. Grant sparingly.

docs.title: Sign in to the Tenant
docs.text: Access the Tenant. Prerequisite: the tenant has been created.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Everything from here on happens inside a single tenant. Sign in with a tenant operator account to begin configuring the PKI.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Open the tenant URL — https://<subdomain>.<your-domain> (e.g. https://tenant.example.com).

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Field Description Required Username or Email Operator login Yes Password Operator password Yes

If the operator account has SSO or Mutual TLS enabled, complete that method instead of a password (see Operators).

docs.title: Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Open the tenant subdomain URL.
  2. Enter your Username or Email and Password.
  3. Click Sign in → you land on the Dashboard.

Important Notes

  • Each tenant displays its own branding (logo, name, theme) on the sign-in screen — see Branding.
  • The top bar offers a theme toggle, language selector, and the account menu (Profile, Logout).

docs.title: Dashboard Overview
docs.text: Access the Tenant. Prerequisite: signed in to the tenant.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The Dashboard is the tenant landing page — a quick read on certificate operations, alerts, and system health before you start configuring.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Dashboard — the default page after login.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Critical Alerts banner (severity-tagged issues).
  • Stat cards — Active Certificates, Pending Requests, CA Coverage, Monthly Issuance.
  • Four tabs:
Tab Contents Overview Issuance trend, distribution by type, system performance, Quick Actions Recent Activity Recent system actions Certificate Authorities CA hierarchy / status System Health Connector health, performance

Recent Activity

Certificate Authorities

System Health

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
• Switch tabs; use Quick Actions (Issue Certificate, Create Template, Configure CA, Review Requests) to jump into workflows.

Important Notes

  • Metrics are tenant-scoped; empty environments show zero/empty series.
  • On a fresh tenant, continue with Roles & Permissions to set up access.

docs.title: Roles & Permissions
docs.text: Access Control. Prerequisite: signed in to the tenant. Set up roles before creating operators, so each operator can be assigned the right role.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Roles bundle fine-grained permissions and (optionally) require approval for protected actions. They are the foundation of the tenant's role-based access control (RBAC).

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Operators & Roles → Roles & Permissions tab.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Create Role button, search, approval-status filter.
  • Role cards — name, permission count, Requires Approval: Yes/No, Assigned Operators, plus View / Edit / Delete.

A predefined system_owner role (full privileges) is seeded per tenant.

docs.title: Fields — Create Role dialog
docs.text: Field Description Required Notes Role name Display name Yes — Description Purpose No — Requires Approval Route this role's protected writes to Approvals No Toggle Permissions Per-permission switches grouped by resource Yes See the full catalog on the API Keys page

docs.title: Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Open Operators & Roles → Roles & Permissions.
  2. Click Create Role.
  3. Enter name/description; set Requires Approval if dual-control is needed.
  4. Toggle the required Permissions.
  5. Save.

Important Notes

  • A role with Requires Approval turns its holders' protected writes into pending approvals.
  • Grant the minimum permissions each role needs.

docs.title: Operators
docs.text: Access Control. Prerequisite: at least one role exists.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Operators are the tenant's user accounts. Here you create them, assign a role, and choose their authentication methods (password, SSO, mutual TLS).

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Operators & Roles → Operator Management tab.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Create Operator button, search, status filter.
  • Operator cards — name, email, status, department, location, last login, created, assigned role, plus View / Edit / Delete.

docs.title: Fields — Create Operator dialog
docs.text: Field Description Required Notes Full Name / Email / Username Identity Yes — Department / Phone / Location Optional details No — Status Active / Inactive No Defaults to Active Role Assigned role Yes From Roles Password (toggle) Allow password login — When on: Password + Confirm required User must create a new password at next login Force reset No Checkbox SSO (toggle) Single sign-on via a configured connector No — Mutual TLS (toggle) Require client-certificate authentication No —

docs.title: Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Open Operators & Roles → Operator Management.
  2. Click Create Operator.
  3. Fill Full Name, Email, Username; choose Role and Status.
  4. Configure Authentication Methods (Password and/or SSO / Mutual TLS).
  5. Click Create.

Important Notes

  • SSO and Mutual TLS are per-operator options enabled here.
  • The last active admin cannot be removed or deactivated (lockout guard).

docs.title: Create Connectors
docs.text: Cryptographic Foundation. Prerequisite: signed in to the tenant. Create the Crypto Engine Connector here first — the next step (Crypto Sources) depends on it.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Connectors are integrations to external services — Crypto Engine (for key storage), Email (SMTP), Syslog, and SIEM — used by crypto sources, notifications, and log export.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Connectors

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Add Connector button.
  • Left panel: connector list with type badge (Crypto Engine / SIEM / Email (SMTP) / Syslog), a Default marker, and Active/Inactive status; each has a Delete control.
  • Right panel: selected connector with tabs.

docs.title: Detail tabs
docs.text:
Tab Contents Configuration Type-specific connection settings Monitoring Health/status Logs Activity log DLQ Dead-letter queue (e.g. failed SIEM pushes)

Monitoring

Logs

DLQ

docs.title: Fields — Add New Connector dialog
docs.text: Field Description Required Notes Connector Type Crypto Engine / SIEM / Email (SMTP) / Syslog Yes Selecting a type reveals its config fields Connector Name Display name Yes — Description Purpose No — Status Active / Inactive No Defaults to Active Default Mark as default for its type No Toggle

docs.title: Step-by-Step — Create the Crypto Engine connector
docs.text:
1. Open Connectors.
  2. Click Add Connector.
  3. Choose Connector Type = Crypto Engine, name it, fill the connection settings.
  4. Click Create Connector.

Important Notes

  • Configuration fields differ per type (SMTP host/port, syslog target, SIEM endpoint, crypto engine settings).
  • Use the DLQ tab to replay failed SIEM/event pushes.

docs.title: Configure Crypto Sources
docs.text: Cryptographic Foundation. Prerequisite: a Crypto Engine connector exists.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Crypto Sources define where cryptographic keys live — an HSM via PKCS#11 or a software key store — backed by a crypto connector. CAs and certificate requests reference a crypto source when generating or using keys.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Crypto Sources

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Add button, search, connector filter, store filter.
  • Table — Name, Store Type (PKCS#11 / SOFTWARE), Connector, Created at, Actions.

docs.title: Fields — Create Crypto Source dialog
docs.text: Field Description Required Notes Name Display name Yes — Connector Backing crypto connector Yes The Crypto Engine Connector created previously Store Type PKCS#11 / SOFTWARE Yes PKCS#11 = HSM-backed; SOFTWARE = software store

docs.title: Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Open Crypto Sources.
  2. Click Add.
  3. Enter Name, select the Connector and Store Type.
  4. Click Create.

Important Notes

  • A crypto source requires a configured Crypto Engine connector.
  • Choose PKCS#11 for HSM-backed keys; SOFTWARE keeps keys in the software store.

docs.title: Create Templates
docs.text: Certificate Templates. Prerequisite: signed in to the tenant. Create templates before building CAs and profiles — both reference a template.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Certificate Templates are reusable blueprints — type, validity, key/signature algorithms, extensions, subject-field and SAN constraints. You typically create a Root CA Template, a Sub CA Template, and one or more End-Entity templates (e.g. TLS Server, OCSP Signing).

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Templates

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Create Template button, search, type filter.
  • Card grid — name, type (Root CA / Sub CA / End Entity), version, validity, key algorithm, signature algorithm, tags, plus View / Edit.

docs.title: Fields — Create Template dialog
docs.text: The dialog has six tabs.

docs.title: General
docs.text: Field Description Required Notes Template Name Display name Yes — Template Type Root CA / Sub CA / End Entity Yes Drives path length and usage Path Length CA path length constraint Yes e.g. "0 (No Sub-CAs)" Validity Value / Unit Default validity Yes e.g. 365 Days Key Algorithms Allowed key algorithms Yes Multi-select Signature Algorithm Signing algorithm Yes e.g. SHA256WithRSA Tags / Description Labels / purpose No —

docs.title: Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Open Templates → Create Template.
  2. On General, set name, type (start with Root CA Template), path length, validity, algorithms.
  3. Configure Extensions, Subject Fields, and SAN Constraints as needed.
  4. Save. Repeat for a Sub CA Template and any End-Entity templates.

Important Notes

  • Subject Fields and SAN Constraints here drive what requesters can enter in the request wizard.
  • Match template type to intended use: Root CA / Sub CA for CAs, End Entity for leaf certs.

docs.title: Create the Root CA
docs.text: Build the CA Hierarchy. Prerequisites: a Root CA Template (Templates) and a Crypto Source for the key.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The Root CA is the self-signed trust anchor at the top of your hierarchy. Create it first; the Sub CA in the next step is signed by it.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Certificate Authorities

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Create CA button (top right).
  • Left panel: searchable CA list with each CA's name and type (Root CA / Sub CA / External CA).
  • Right panel: selected CA summary (Status, Template, Key Algorithm, Signed By, Validity, Serial Number) with Download Certificate and Revoke CA.

docs.title: Fields — Create CA dialog (Root)
docs.text: Field Description Required Notes CA Name Display name (e.g. Root CA 01) Yes — CA Type Root Yes Root = self-signed trust anchor Template CA template Yes Choose your Root CA Template

docs.title: Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Open Certificate Authorities → Create CA.
  2. Enter a CA Name, set CA Type = Root, choose the Root CA Template.
  3. Click Create CA, then complete key generation (select the Crypto Source) and self-signing.

Important Notes

  • A Root CA signs itself (Signed By: Self-signed).
  • Key generation may require a Key Ceremony / Two-Person Control.

Security Warning

The Root CA is your trust anchor — protect its key (prefer an HSM/PKCS#11 crypto source).

docs.title: Create the Sub CA (Issuing CA)
docs.text: Build the CA Hierarchy. Prerequisites: a Root CA, a Sub CA Template (Templates), and a Crypto Source.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The Sub CA (Issuing CA) is signed by the Root CA and does the day-to-day certificate issuance — keeping the Root offline/protected. End-entity certificates chain to it.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Certificate Authorities → Create CA

docs.title: Fields — Create CA dialog (Sub)
docs.text: Field Description Required Notes CA Name Display name (e.g. Sub CA 01) Yes — CA Type Intermediate (Issuing / Sub CA) Yes — Template CA template Yes Choose your Sub CA Template Signed By Parent CA Yes Select the Root CA created previously

docs.title: Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Open Certificate Authorities → Create CA.
  2. Enter a CA Name, set CA Type = Intermediate, choose the Sub CA Template.
  3. Set Signed By = Root CA.
  4. Click Create CA, then complete key generation (select a Crypto Source) and signing by the Root.

Important Notes

  • You can create multiple Sub CAs (e.g. one per certificate purpose).
  • Next: configure the CA (CRL, OCSP/AIA distribution), then set up a Validation Authority.

docs.title: Configure the CA (Keys, CRL, Distribution)
docs.text: Build the CA Hierarchy. Prerequisite: a Root CA and/or Sub CA exists.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Once a CA exists, configure how it manages keys, publishes revocation (CRL), and advertises validation/issuer endpoints (OCSP / AIA). Select a CA in the list to expose its configuration tabs.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Certificate Authorities → select a CA → tabs.

docs.title: Key Configuration
docs.text: Key pair details — Key Name, Crypto Source, Key Algorithm — and key operations.

docs.title: Certificate Data
docs.text: The CA certificate's subject DN and content.

docs.title: Directives
docs.text: CA policy directives.

docs.title: CRL Settings
docs.text: Certificate Revocation List configuration (publication cadence, distribution point).

docs.title: Distribution
docs.text: OCSP responder URL, OCSP service default URI, CA Issuer default URI, Publish AIA, and Allow CA certificate for OCSP signing.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
• Per-tab Save — persist configuration.
  • Download Certificate — export the CA certificate.
  • Revoke CA — revoke the CA (invalidates everything it issued; irreversible).

docs.title: Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Open Certificate Authorities and select the CA.
  2. Review Key Configuration (confirm the crypto source/key).
  3. Configure CRL Settings (publication) and Distribution (OCSP/AIA URLs, Publish AIA).
  4. Save each tab.

Important Notes

  • OCSP responses are served by a Validation Authority.

Critical Warning

Revoking a CA cascades to all certificates that CA issued — use with extreme care.

docs.title: Configure a Validation Authority (OCSP)
docs.text: Validation. Prerequisites: a CA and an OCSP signing certificate. Requires the VA license module.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: A Validation Authority (VA) is an OCSP responder that answers real-time certificate-status queries for a CA, and keeps in sync with the CA's revocation state.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Validation Authorities

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Three tabs plus a Create Validation Authority button.

docs.title: Validation Authorities
docs.text:
VA list + configuration form + per-CA Sync Status.

Field Description Name / Description Responder identity Certificate Authority CA whose status this VA answers for OCSP Signing Certificate Certificate used to sign OCSP responses Response validity / Max-Age (seconds) Freshness / cache hints ResponderID KEYHASH / NAME Non-issued certificate behavior Response for unknown serials Include chain / signing cert / nonce Response options Require signed requests / Omit revocation reason (CABF) Compliance toggles

docs.title: External CAs
docs.text: External CAs whose status this VA serves.

docs.title: Sync Diagnostics
docs.text: CA→VA replay tools (Source, Batch Size, Resume/Reset, Run Full Resync, Push One Batch) and a Dead-Letter Queue with Replay Pending.

docs.title: Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Open Validation Authorities → Create Validation Authority and complete the dialog.
  2. Select the VA, set Certificate Authority, OCSP Signing Certificate, validity, and response options.
  3. Click Save. Use Sync This VA / Sync Diagnostics if status is stale.

Important Notes

  • A VA depends on a response CA and an OCSP signing certificate.
  • Use Sync Diagnostics when events are stale or the DLQ has pending items.

docs.title: Create Certificate Profiles
docs.text: Issuance. Prerequisites: a Sub CA (issuing CA) and a Template.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: A profile combines a template with an issuing CA and an approval mode. Profiles are what requesters choose when requesting a certificate; they define issuance policy.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Certificate Profiles

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Create Profile button, search, type/approval filters.
  • Card grid — name, status, approval mode, Certificate Type, Issuing CA, Validity, Certificates Issued, Template, plus View Details / Edit Profile.

docs.title: Fields — Create Profile dialog
docs.text: Field Description Required Notes Profile Name Display name Yes — Certificate Type e.g. Server Auth / Code Signing Yes — Description Purpose No — Issuing CA CA that signs certificates from this profile Yes Your Sub CA Approval Mode Auto / Manual No Manual → routes to Approvals Certificate Template The single template defining key usages/extensions Yes From Templates

docs.title: Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Open Certificate Profiles → Create Profile.
  2. Enter Profile Name and Certificate Type.
  3. Choose Issuing CA (Sub CA), Approval Mode, and one Certificate Template.
  4. Click Create Profile.

Important Notes

  • All key usages/extensions derive from the chosen template.
  • Approval Mode = Manual sends requests to Approvals.

docs.title: Request & Issue a Certificate
docs.text: Issuance. Prerequisite: a Certificate Profile.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Request (and, when auto-approved, issue) a certificate through a guided wizard that enforces the selected profile's template constraints. This is the payoff of the configuration flow.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Certificate Requests → Request Certificate

docs.title: Step 1 — Select Certificate Profile
docs.text: Choose a profile card (each shows Template, Issuing CA, Certificate Type).

docs.title: Steps 2–4 — Subject, SAN, CSR
docs.text:
Fill the allowed Subject fields and required SAN entries (the profile's template controls which are allowed/required), then provide the CSR.

CSR options — Upload CSR (paste/upload PEM) or Generate Key + CSR:

Field (Generate Key + CSR) Description Required Crypto Source Where the key is generated Yes Key Algorithm / Key Size Key parameters Yes Key Name Key identifier Yes Key Password Protects the key Optional

Submit & Generate Certificate stays disabled until all required data is present.

docs.title: Reviewing requests
docs.text:
Certificate Requests → Requests List lists every request with Status and Approval Mode.

A row's View shows full request details (subject, SAN, CSR PEM with Download).

docs.title: Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Open Request Certificate and pick a profile.
  2. Fill the allowed Subject fields and required SAN entries.
  3. Upload CSR or Generate Key + CSR.
  4. Click Submit & Generate Certificate.

Important Notes

  • The profile/template controls which subject and SAN fields you may set.

docs.title: Manage Certificates
docs.text: Issuance. Prerequisite: certificates have been issued.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The Certificates module is the inventory of issued certificates — search, inspect, download, and revoke them across the tenant's CAs.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Certificates

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Search, status filter (All / Active / Revoked / Expired), Clear.
  • Table — Subject, Serial Number, Issuer, Status, Valid From, Valid To, Actions.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
• View — full certificate details (chain, extensions, key usage).
  • Download — export the certificate.
  • Revoke — revoke an active certificate (requires cert.revoke; may route through Approvals).

docs.title: Step-by-Step — Revoke a certificate
docs.text:
1. Open Certificates, search for the certificate.
  2. Open its row Actions → Revoke.
  3. Select a reason and confirm.

Important Notes

  • New certificates are created via Request Certificate, not here.

Warning

Revocation is irreversible for trust purposes — confirm the correct certificate first.

docs.title: Approvals
docs.text: Operations & Governance. Prerequisite: a role with Requires Approval enabled (otherwise the queue stays empty).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The Approvals queue is where protected actions submitted by approval-required roles are reviewed. Approvers accept or reject them, giving dual-control over sensitive operations.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Approvals

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Refresh button, search, status filter.
  • Requests list of pending and historical approvals (empty when nothing is waiting).

docs.title: How approvals are created
docs.text: When an operator whose role requires approval performs a protected write, it is not applied immediately — it becomes a pending approval here. An approver then Approves (applies it) or Rejects (discards it).

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
• Refresh — reload the queue.
  • View — inspect a request and its before/after change.
  • Approve — apply the action (requires approval.approve).
  • Reject — discard it (requires approval.reject).

docs.title: Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Open Approvals and filter to Pending.
  2. Open a request and review the proposed change.
  3. Click Approve or Reject.

Important Notes

  • Which roles require approval is set per role in Roles & Permissions.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: Operations & Governance. Prerequisite: a delivery connector (e.g. Email (SMTP)).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Configure automated alerts and reminder schedules (e.g. expiry reminders) delivered through a connector to chosen recipients.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Notifications

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Create Notification button, search, connector/status filters.
  • Table — Name, Connector, Days, Created at, Frequency, Status, Actions.

docs.title: Fields — Create Notification dialog
docs.text: Field Description Required Notes Notification name Display name Yes — Connector Delivery channel Yes From Connectors Status Active / Inactive Yes — Scheduler type Schedule basis Yes — Frequency e.g. hourly / daily Yes — Recipient emails Explicit recipients No Empty = every active operator Description Optional note No —

docs.title: Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Open Notifications → Create Notification.
  2. Enter Name, choose Connector, Status, Scheduler type, Frequency.
  3. Optionally add Recipient emails.
  4. Click Create Notification.

Important Notes

  • Empty Recipient emails broadcasts to all active operators.
  • Delivery depends on a healthy connector — check Connectors → Monitoring.

docs.title: API Keys
docs.text: Operations & Governance. Prerequisite: signed in to the tenant.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: API Keys grant scoped, programmatic access to the tenant's API — with fine-grained permissions, rate limits, optional IP allow-listing, and an expiry — for automation and integrations without operator credentials.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: API Keys

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: • Generate API Key button, search, status filter.

docs.title: Fields — Generate API Key dialog
docs.text: Field Description Required Notes Key name Display name Yes — Status Active / Inactive No Defaults to Active Expiry Lifetime (e.g. 30 days) No — Description Optional note No — Rate limit requests Max requests per window Yes Defaults to 100 Rate limit window Minute / Hour / … No Defaults to Hour IP Whitelist Allowed IPs/CIDRs No e.g. 192.168.1.10, 10.0.0.0/24 Permissions Per-permission switches grouped by resource (+ Select All) Yes See catalog below

docs.title: Permission catalog
docs.text:
The assignable scopes (also used by Roles), grouped by resource:

  • Certificates: Cert View, Cert Revoke
  • Certificate payloads: View, Create, Delete
  • Certificate authorities: Ca View, Ca Configure, Ca Key Ceremony, Ca Crl Manage
  • Validation authorities: Va View, Va Configure
  • Crypto tokens: Token View, Token Manage, Token Delete
  • Crypto sources: View, Create, Delete
  • Templates: View, Create, Edit, Delete
  • Profiles: View, Create, Edit, Delete
  • Certificate requests: View, Create, Issue, Keypair
  • Connectors: View, Create, Edit, Delete
  • Notifications: View, Create, Edit, Delete
  • Approvals: View, Approve, Reject
  • Audit: View, Create, Delete
  • Access logs: View
  • SIEM: Read, Manage
  • General settings: View, Edit
  • Roles: Role View, Role Manage, Role Member View, Role Member Manage
  • Operators: View, Create, Edit, Delete

docs.title: Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Open API Keys → Generate API Key.
  2. Enter Key name, set Expiry, Rate limit, optional IP Whitelist.
  3. Toggle the required Permissions (or Select All).
  4. Click Generate API Key and copy the secret immediately.

Important Notes

  • Grant minimum permissions; use IP Whitelist and short Expiry for tighter control.

Security Warning

The API Key secret is shown only once upon creation — store it securely.

docs.title: Logs (Audit Trail)
docs.text: Operations & Governance. Prerequisite: signed in to the tenant.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The Logs module is the immutable record of system activity — every request and protected action with actor, target, source IP, and outcome — for security review and compliance.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Logs

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Refresh button, search, Clear.
  • Table — Sr#, Action, Target, Time, IP Address, User Agent, Status (Pass/Fail), View.

docs.title: Detail (View)
docs.text: A row's View opens the full entry — request/response detail, payload, and error trace on failures.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
• Refresh — reload entries.
  • Search — filter by action or actor.
  • View — open a single entry's full detail.

docs.title: Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Open Logs and search for the action or actor.
  2. Click View to see full request/response and any error trace.

Important Notes

  • Retention/rotation is governed by Log Rotation.
  • Programmatic SIEM export uses a SIEM connector + SIEM permissions.

docs.title: General Settings
docs.text: System Settings & Profile. Prerequisite: signed in to the tenant.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Tenant-level application settings — identity, URLs, logo, and syslog enterprise number — that shape how the tenant presents itself and integrates with logging.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Settings → General Settings

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Typical settings: application name, company name, application/admin URLs, logo upload, and the syslog Enterprise PEN (RFC 5424 Private Enterprise Number).

docs.title: Actions
docs.text: • Update fields and Save; upload a logo where supported.

docs.title: Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Open Settings → General Settings.
  2. Update the desired fields.
  3. Save.

Important Notes

  • Tenant-scoped; they do not affect other tenants.
  • Theme/colors are on Branding; log behavior on Log Rotation.

docs.title: Log Rotation & Signing
docs.text: System Settings & Profile. Prerequisite: for log signing, a Crypto Source.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Configure how audit/system logs are written, rotated, signed, and (optionally) archived to cloud storage — supporting retention policy and log integrity.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Settings → Log Rotation

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Typical sections:

  • File logging — enable, log path, rotation mode (size/time), max size / backup count / interval.
  • Log signing — enable, algorithm, signing crypto source + key alias, verification certificate.
  • Cloud storage (where available) — provider, bucket/region/prefix, credentials.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text: • Update logging config and Save; upload a signing/verification certificate; test cloud storage where offered.

docs.title: Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Open Settings → Log Rotation.
  2. Set the file-logging rotation policy.
  3. Optionally enable Log signing and select a Crypto Source/key.
  4. Optionally configure Cloud storage. Save.

Important Notes

  • Log signing relies on a crypto source for the signing key.
  • These settings govern retention of the Logs trail.

docs.title: Branding
docs.text: System Settings & Profile. Prerequisite: signed in to the tenant.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Customize the tenant's visual identity — theme colors and appearance — so the portal matches the organization. Branding is per-tenant and shows on the sign-in screen and throughout the app.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Settings → Branding

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A theme customizer for the tenant's colors (primary/secondary/accents/text) and related appearance options.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text: • Adjust theme colors and Save; preview where supported.

docs.title: Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Open Settings → Branding.
  2. Set the theme colors.
  3. Save to apply across the tenant.

Important Notes

  • Branding is isolated per tenant; it never affects other tenants or the Super Admin portal.
  • Logo and application name are set on General Settings.

docs.title: User Profile & MFA
docs.text: System Settings & Profile. Prerequisite: signed in to the tenant.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Your personal account page — review your identity and role, see your effective permissions, and manage security (MFA, client-certificate auth) and basic profile details.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Profile, or the account menu → Profile.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Identity card — name, @username, status, role badge, Email, Department, Role.
  • Account — Last Login, Created, 2FA (TOTP) state, Client Certificate Auth state.
  • Permissions — your effective permissions (total), grouped by resource with counts.
  • Edit Profile button.

docs.title: Fields — Edit Profile dialog
docs.text: Editable personal details (full name, department, phone, location). Role and permissions are managed by an administrator in Operators & Roles.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
• Edit Profile — update your details.
  • Enable/disable 2FA (TOTP) and Client Certificate Auth.

docs.title: Step-by-Step
docs.text:
1. Open Profile.
  2. Check Account for MFA / client-cert status.
  3. Review Permissions to confirm your effective rights.

Important Notes

  • 2FA (TOTP) and Client Certificate Auth are Disabled by default — enabling MFA is recommended.
  • To change your role/permissions, contact a tenant administrator.

docs.title: CA Deployment Guide
docs.text: This guide walks through installing the Certificate Authority (CA) platform on an in-house server. The backend services and frontend run as Docker containers orchestrated by Docker Compose.

docs.title: 1. Minimum Requirements
docs.text: Resource Specification Operating System Ubuntu 24.04 LTS CPU 4–8 cores Memory (RAM) 8–16 GB Disk Space 50 GB+ Required Software Docker, Docker Compose, NGINX

docs.title: 2. Architecture Overview
docs.text:
The CA platform is composed of the following containers (see docker-compose.yml):

  • ca – The FastAPI CA API service (host port 28000 → container 8000). Issues and manages certificates, CAs, profiles, and templates.
  • ocsp – The OCSP responder / Validation Authority service (host port 28001), run in OCSP_ONLY mode.
  • celery_worker – Background worker for CRL generation and OCSP sync tasks.
  • celery_beat – Scheduler for periodic tasks (CRL publishing, OCSP sync).
  • postgres – PostgreSQL 16 database (internal only by default).
  • redis – Redis 7 broker/result backend for Celery (internal only by default).

The web application (frontend) is deployed separately and points at the CA API via its config.json.

docs.title: 3. Docker Installation
docs.text:
Install Docker Engine and the Compose plugin:

# Add Docker's official GPG key
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install ca-certificates curl
sudo install -m 0755 -d /etc/apt/keyrings
sudo curl -fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg -o /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc
sudo chmod a+r /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc

# Add the repository to Apt sources
echo \
  "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc] https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu \
  $(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION_CODENAME") stable" | \
  sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.list > /dev/null
sudo apt-get update

# Install Docker Engine and Compose
sudo apt-get install docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io docker-buildx-plugin docker-compose-plugin -y

# Allow Docker without sudo
sudo groupadd docker
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER
newgrp docker

docs.title: 4. DNS Configuration
docs.text:
Create DNS entries for your CA environment (replace YOURDOMAIN.com):

ca.YOURDOMAIN.com        # Web application (frontend)
api.ca.YOURDOMAIN.com    # CA API backend
ocsp.ca.YOURDOMAIN.com   # OCSP responder
crl.ca.YOURDOMAIN.com    # CRL distribution

docs.title: 5. NGINX & TLS
docs.text:
Install NGINX as a reverse proxy and obtain TLS certificates (e.g. Let's Encrypt via Certbot):

sudo apt install nginx -y
sudo apt install certbot python3-certbot-nginx -y
sudo certbot certonly --standalone -d ca.YOURDOMAIN.com -d api.ca.YOURDOMAIN.com -d ocsp.ca.YOURDOMAIN.com -d crl.ca.YOURDOMAIN.com

Configure NGINX server blocks to proxy:

  • api.ca.YOURDOMAIN.com → http://127.0.0.1:28000
  • ocsp.ca.YOURDOMAIN.com → http://127.0.0.1:28001
  • ca.YOURDOMAIN.com → the frontend container (port 8080)

docs.title: 6. Backend Configuration (.env)
docs.text:
Copy the environment template and populate it. Never commit .env.

cd dlabs-ca
cp .env.example .env

Set the required values:

  • Application: APP_NAME, APP_ENV (prod for production), DEBUG=false.
  • Security (required):
    • JWT_SECRET_KEY — generate: python -c "import secrets;print(secrets.token_urlsafe(48))"
    • KEY_PASSWORD_FERNET_KEY — generate: python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet;print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"
  • Database: POSTGRES_DB, POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_PASSWORD (use unique non-default credentials).
  • Network: CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS (e.g. https://ca.YOURDOMAIN.com) and ALLOWED_HOSTS. Wildcards are forbidden in production.
  • CRL / OCSP: CRL_PUBLISH_BASE_URL (e.g. https://crl.ca.YOURDOMAIN.com) and OCSP_BASE_URL (e.g. https://ocsp.ca.YOURDOMAIN.com/api/ocsp).
  • Logging: LOG_TO_FILE, LOG_FILE_PATH, rotation settings, and optional LOG_SIGNING_*.

In production the configuration enforces: DEBUG=false, no wildcard CORS/hosts, and OCSP_SYNC_VERIFY_TLS=true.

docs.title: 7. Licensing
docs.text:
A license file issued by Dictalabs is required for the CA API service. Generate the system UUID and share it to obtain your license:

sudo ./scripts/get-system-uuid.sh   # if provided with your package

Place the license file in the license/ directory (mounted into the containers as ca_license).

docs.title: 8. Start the Backend
docs.text:
From the dlabs-ca directory:

docker compose pull   # if using prebuilt images
docker compose up -d

Database migrations (Alembic) run on startup. Verify the containers:

docker ps -a

View logs for a service (stop with Ctrl+C):

docker logs -f dlabs-ca
docker logs -f ca_ocsp
docker logs -f ca_celery_worker
docker logs -f ca_celery_beat

docs.title: 9. Frontend (Web Application) Configuration
docs.text:
Deploy the CA web application package and point it at the backend API. Edit config.json:

{
  "API_BASE_URL": "https://api.ca.YOURDOMAIN.com/api/v1",
  "PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL": "https://api.ca.YOURDOMAIN.com"
}

Start the frontend container:

docker compose up -d

docs.title: 10. Verification
docs.text:
After deployment:

  • Access the CA web app at https://ca.YOURDOMAIN.com and sign in (see Home → Login).
  • Confirm the API health endpoint responds at https://api.ca.YOURDOMAIN.com/health.
  • Confirm the OCSP service responds at https://ocsp.ca.YOURDOMAIN.com.

Once signed in, proceed to create your first Certificate Authority.
